טוב Verbum in tempore suo dictum quàm bonum est? Sensus
est, facile homines sibi in iis, quæ loquuntur, placere & blandiri:
sed illos demum omne punctum ferre, qui verba בעתו ἐν εὐσχήμονι
καιρῷ[?] opportuno tempore, adeoque præsenti tempori congruentia
fundunt. Tametsi vero sapientiam illam & rite loquendi regulam
admirari, quàm sequi & exequi proclivius est: bonum tamen fa-
ctum fore confidimus, si celeusmatis hujus memores, sermonem
nostrum exulceratis hisce, in quibus ecclesia passim manus Dei gra-
viter ferientis pondere pressa, tristem ætatem agit, temporibus ac-
commodaverimus. Cumque in omnium jam propatulo sit, ulti-
mam illam Dei patientiam, ob impletam peccatorum mundi, in o-
mnium scelerum licentiam projecti, mensuram, paulatim abrumpi,
& justa ejusdem judicia à domo ejus cœptari, si de Divinis judiciis
commentationem instituerimus, ad novos casus temporum institu-
ti, consiliorumque nostrorum rationes nonnihil accommodatas fo-
re, nemo forte pius & æquus rerum æstimator inficias ibit.
II. Sunt autem JUDICIA DEI Opera ipsius, quæ in execu-
tione justitiæ suæ, tanquam universalis judex totius mundi, ob gra-
via peccata, quando lubet, sapienter, juste, ad gloriam nominis sui,
electorum salutem, & justam reproborum damnationem exercet.

page.notes: Printed "Pro-verb." and "ju-dicium" and "Iudicia Dei definiuntur." run over line ends; hyphens kept as printed. The Greek word(s) between "ἐν" and "καιρῷ" in paragraph I are hard to read at this resolution; the reading is doubtful and marked [?]. The Hebrew order in the Job line is read from the scan and may be inexact. Catchword "ris" at bottom right is faint and marked [?]. Long s printed as s is written as s. Printed "quàm" kept with its grave accent. The last line of paragraph II ends with a printed hyphen ("furo-") continued at the foot as "ris" (catchword).
